revises.relationship: NARROW REVISION. R2 is retained unmodified as history and was accepted IN SUBSTANCE by the owner, including its proposed terminal outcome token. R3 revises R2 ONLY for the INADMISSIBLE / attempt-consumption semantics. Every other methodology decision is carried through unchanged.
whatR3Changes: The terminal outcome token ACCEPT / REJECT / INADMISSIBLE is APPROVED for disclosure and moves from additionsRequiringOwnerConfirmationAtFreeze into the permitted surface. The attempt consumption state CONSUMED / NOT_CONSUMED joins it. Both are procedural, not item-level.

A new section O freezes SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED - a monotonic, irreversible boundary that is the Methodology V2 name for the ALREADY-FROZEN F0V Class C rule (PROVIDER_REQUEST_OR_SEMANTIC_EXECUTION_OBSERVED), not a new invention.
R2's claim that an INADMISSIBLE study 'measured nothing about the candidate' is WITHDRAWN as a general statement. It is true only PRE-semantically.
DEV_CONFIRM budget: PRE_SEMANTIC_INADMISSIBLE is NOT_CONSUMED and may retry the byte-identical candidate; POST_SEMANTIC_INADMISSIBLE is CONSUMED and may never re-run against that generation.

A realised-denominator failure derived from candidate outputs - the G3 precision case above all - is POST-SEMANTIC by definition and ALWAYS consumes the attempt. It is explicitly not a harness-only failure.
FINAL_HOLDOUT: a pre-semantic INADMISSIBLE does NOT retire it; crossing SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED retires it irreversibly at terminal closure regardless of ACCEPT, REJECT or INADMISSIBLE.
The stability execution is governed by the same boundary, with no return of N = 5 replacement logic.

R2's statement that all of S1-S7 are properties of the harness and corpus alone is CORRECTED. Each precondition gains an evaluability classification (PRE_SEMANTIC / POST_SEMANTIC / BOTH); the count stays seven and no precondition changes what it requires.

CORPUS_OPTION_B and every organisation, document and denominator number

designsNotSelected.D2_A: POINT_TARGET_ONLY. REJECTED. It makes no confidence claim at all, so no true rate is ever established or excluded. Retained in R1 only as the honest label for the status quo.
designsNotSelected.D2_B: TARGET_PLUS_EXACT_BOUND at the threshold itself. REJECTED on power and cost: acceptance at a true rate exactly equal to the owner own frozen target cannot exceed alpha at ANY denominator, and 80% acceptance for a genuinely 0.98 candidate needs 234 gold unit pages in EACH gated split.
designsNotSelected.D2_C: TARGET_PLUS_FIXED_UNCERTAINTY_MARGIN without cluster deflation. sectionC_D2_certificationDesign.theRuleInOneSentence: For each gate: the point estimate meets the frozen threshold AND the exact one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound, computed on the design-effect-deflated denominator of THAT GATE OWN numerator and denominator, meets that gate certification level - and the gate passed the section-K feasibility precondition at both its planned and its realised denominator.

frozenParameters.clusteringUnitIsNeverThePage: A page is not an independent top-level sample. Pages of one organisation share a template, a vocabulary, an information architecture and an author.
frozenParameters.rhoRule: rho = max(RHO_FLOOR, observed ANOVA intraclass correlation over the split organisations)
frozenParameters.rhoEscalationOnly: the observed ICC may only RAISE the assumed value, never lower it. An ICC estimated from few clusters is noisy, and a noisy estimate that can only shrink the effective denominator is safe while one that can enlarge it is not.
frozenParameters.rhoFloorClassification: MECHANICAL SAFETY BOUND, NOT A CALIBRATED VALUE. It is not a measurement of this corpus: the existing 49-item DEVELOPMENT set has 12 organisations and no recorded organisation-level ICC.
frozenParameters.cbarRule: cbar is the average number of items THIS GATE OWN denominator contributes per organisation - computed SEPARATELY FOR EACH GATE, never the split average. A gate whose denominator is a sparse subset of the sample (G3 unitPagePrecision, whose denominator is the items the candidate answered UNIT_PAGE) is clustered far less than the sample it was drawn from, and charging it the sample design effect would overcharge it.

roundingRule.bothDirectionsAreConservative: For a lower-bound (higher-is-better) gate, flooring trials shrinks the information and flooring successes lowers the observed rate; both move the bound DOWN, against the candidate. For an upper-bound (lower-is-better) gate the event count is CEILED instead, because flooring events there would move the bound DOWN and therefore IN FAVOUR of the candidate - the opposite of conservative.

frozenParameters.honestLimitation: the bound is EXACT conditional on the effective denominator; the effective denominator itself rests on the ICC. This is an approximation, stated as one. R1 clustered-coverage simulation measures how good it is rather than assuming it.

theSixGates.denominator: every evaluated item in the split (SET_P and SET_R together)
theSixGates.boundReported: the exact point rate and its exact one-sided 95% lower bound are REPORTED FOR INFORMATION alongside, and are explicitly NON-BINDING. The zero-tolerance rule is not replaced by a confidence-bound rule.
theSixGates.whyZeroToleranceRatherThanARateGate: Certifying 0.99 needs 299 flawless items undeflated and 509 under a design effect of 1.7 - and at 509, 600 and 700 the deflated critical count still EQUALS the denominator. The gate first tolerates a SINGLE error at 473 items undeflated, and at 805 under a design effect of 1.7. At every corpus size this project could acquire, a 0.99 gate IS a zero-tolerance gate. Naming it zero-tolerance removes a threshold that implies a tolerance the denominator never supplies. That is arithmetic, not a policy preference.
theSixGates.notRelabelledAsAStructuralPrecondition: D6 requires G1 to remain one of the six SEMANTIC GATES, and it does: it is a gate with a zero-tolerance rule, not a structural precondition.

theSixGates.denominator: gold UNIT_PAGE items in SET_R of the split
items in SET_P answered UNIT_PAGE by a validator-accepted result
items whose GOLD verdict is UNIT_PAGE in SET_R (the 2D2C convention, adopted explicitly; resolves d11)

theSixGates.directionOfUncertainty: UPPER confidence bound. This is an upper-bound problem, not a lower-bound problem: a ceiling gate asks whether the true rate is AT MOST X, and a lower bound would certify the opposite direction. Using an LCB here would be a sign error, not a conservatism choice. The original proposal five-row feasibility table omitted this gate entirely.

certificationTolerancesCanBeStricterThan.observedAtTheHistoricalDenominator: At n = 49, G6 point tolerance is 7 events while its certification tolerance at either ceiling is 2: an observation of 7/49 = 0.1429 PASSES the point gate and FAILS certification, because the upper bound there is 0.2516. This is why the rule requires BOTH conditions and why neither is redundant in general.
certificationTolerancesCanBeStricterThan.classification: METHODOLOGICAL CONTEXT ONLY. No candidate needs-review rate is evaluated anywhere in this document.

sectionE_samplingContract.purpose: Owner instruction section 5: Option B must be fully machine-checkable. Every rule below is deterministic, content-derived and testable. Where R1 left decidable prose, R2 states the exact decision an implementation must make.

globalDeterminismRule.rule: Every selection in this section is a deterministic function of committed content. No pseudo-random number generator is used at any point, so there is no seed to record and no machine-dependent permutation to reproduce.
globalDeterminismRule.whyNotSeeded: A content-derived rank (a SHA-256 over a committed identifier) is reproducible by anyone holding the committed frame, with no shared PRNG implementation, no language-specific stream and no seed to transcribe. A seeded PRNG would add a dependency on an exact generator without adding determinism this does not already have.
globalDeterminismRule.rankDefinition: To rank a set by key K: compute sha256(K) for each element, render as LOWER-CASE HEX, and sort ASCENDING by that 64-character string under plain lexicographic byte comparison. Ties are impossible unless two elements share K, which the frame forbids.
globalDeterminismRule.saltedRankDefinition: Where a rank must be independent of another rank over the same elements, the key is salted: sha256(SALT + ":" + K). Salts are frozen literals declared in this document. A salt exists so that two selections over the same population are not the same permutation; it is not a secret.

rules.question: organisation sampling frame
rules.rule: An organisation is FRAME-ELIGIBLE iff it has at least one STRUCTURALLY_VALID website_claims row OR at least one live, un-revoked orgunit_root_promotions row, AND it contributes no item to the historical 49-item DEVELOPMENT set, AND it appears in no earlier Methodology V2 generation corpus.
rules.exactness: The frame is ENUMERATED IN FULL and committed, with its own content hash, BEFORE any draw and BEFORE any acquisition. The committed frame is the denominator of every claim about representativeness.
rules.whyCountryBlind: This repository stores no country, locale or market signal for research purposes and must not acquire one here. Country is recorded per organisation as a REPORTED stratum only (SD7) and is never a sampling constraint, a gate or a reweighting key.

rules.question: organisation split assignment
rules.rule: Rank every FRAME-ELIGIBLE organisation by sha256(eche_row_key) ascending. Walk that rank from position 0, admitting each organisation to the SELECTION LIST, until the selection list holds ACQUISITION_TARGET_ORGANISATIONS = 110 entries; continue walking to admit a further ACQUISITION_RESERVE_ORGANISATIONS = 40 entries to the RESERVE LIST, in the same rank order. Both lists are committed together, BEFORE acquisition begins. Assign the split of the organisation at selection index i (0-based) as SPLIT_ASSIGNMENT_CYCLE_V2_R2[i mod 22].
rules.whyTwentyTwo: The target ratio 20 : 45 : 45 reduces exactly to 4 : 9 : 9, which sums to 22, and 110 / 22 = 5. Five repetitions of the cycle therefore yield EXACTLY 20 / 45 / 45 with no remainder rule, no rounding and no discretion. The cycle is also maximally interleaved: no two consecutive positions carry the same split, and every 22-position block contains all three splits.
rules.exactCountsAreStructural: The counts are a property of the cycle and the total, not of the data. A test asserts 20 / 45 / 45 by construction.
rules.assignmentIsLabelBlindDifficultyBlindRes: sha256(eche_row_key) is a content hash of a source-row identity. It cannot encode a label, a difficulty, a model result or an acquisition outcome, because none of those exists when it is computed.
rules.replacementRule: If an organisation on the selection list is NOT ACQUISITION_SUCCESSFUL (SD9), it is replaced by the next unused RESERVE organisation in rank order, and the replacement INHERITS the replaced organisation selection index and therefore its split. Every replacement is recorded with both eche_row_keys and the reason. This keeps 20 / 45 / 45 exact and keeps the split assignment independent of acquisition outcome.
rules.reserveExhaustionIsARefusal: If the reserve is exhausted before 110 successful organisations exist, the corpus freeze is REFUSED. A smaller corpus is never silently accepted, because every denominator in section D depends on the count.

rules.question: page sampling within an organisation
rules.rule: SET_P: from the organisation acquired, policy-authorised, deduplicated pages (SD6), take the first SET_P_MAX_PAGES_PER_ORGANISATION = 8 by salted rank sha256("SET_P_V2_R2:" + documentSha256) ascending, with NO class filtering of any kind. SET_R: from the same deduplicated pool, take the first SET_R_MAX_PAGES_PER_ORGANISATION = 4 by the FROZEN deterministic Track A/B signal score descending, tie-broken by sha256("SET_R_V2_R2:" + documentSha256) ascending.
rules.setRRankIsCandidateIndependent: The Track A/B score comes from ORGUNIT_SIGNAL_RULE_VERSION orgunit-signal-rules-v1, a frozen, pure, candidate-independent ruleset. No model output, gold label or candidate result participates in the ranking.
rules.setPAndSetRMayOverlap: A page may be drawn into both samples. The evaluation set is their union deduplicated by goldId, and the item is inferred ONCE; each gate then reads it only from the sample that gate is defined on (section F). Double inference is forbidden - it would make one item two observations.

rules.question: maximum page contribution from one organisation
rules.rule: Per organisation, per split: at most 8 pages in SET_P and at most 4 in SET_R. In addition, no organisation may contribute more than ORGANISATION_GATE_SHARE_CAP = 1/10 of ANY gate realised denominator. If the per-sample caps alone do not secure the 1/10 condition, that organisation contribution to the offending gate denominator is TRUNCATED by the same deterministic rank until the condition holds, and the truncation is recorded.
rules.checkedTwice: mechanically at freeze time on planned denominators, and again at scoring time on realised denominators
rules.capRationale: Items per organisation is a first-order lever on error control, not a convenience: at ICC 0.2 the same item count loses about five times its nominal error control at 8 pages per organisation and about three times at 4. SET_R carries the two highest-stakes gates and gets the tighter cap.

rules.question: UNIT_PAGE enrichment
rules.rule: UNIT_PAGE enrichment happens ONLY in SET_R, ONLY through the frozen Track A/B rank of SD3, and NEVER by consulting a gold label, a model output or a candidate result. SET_R is used ONLY for metrics conditional on the GOLD class (G2 recall, G4 unit-type). The realised enrichment factor - the ratio of gold UNIT_PAGE share in SET_R to that in SET_P - is COMPUTED AND RECORDED with the corpus, and is never used to reweight a gate.
rules.enrichmentByGoldLabelIsForbidden: Selecting SET_R by gold label would make G2 recall a measurement of the selector rather than of the candidate, and would make the enrichment factor unknowable in production.
rules.shortfallRule: If a gated split realises fewer than 100 gold UNIT_PAGE items in SET_R, SET_R is EXTENDED by continuing down the same frozen Track A/B rank - never by relaxing the per-organisation cap and never by selecting on gold - until 100 is reached or the organisation pool is exhausted. If it cannot be reached, the corpus freeze is REFUSED.

rules.question: hard-negative enrichment
rules.rule: HARD NEGATIVES ARE NOT ENRICHED. They are taken as they fall in the prevalence-faithful SET_P, because G5 denominator must stay meaningful as a share of a production-like sample. The frozen requirement is a MINIMUM COUNT, met by SET_P size, not by a filter: at least 155 gold hard negatives in SET_P per gated split.
rules.shortfallRule: If a gated split realises fewer than 155 gold hard negatives in SET_P, SET_P is EXTENDED by continuing down the same frozen salted rank of SD3 - with no class filtering, so the extension stays prevalence-faithful - until 155 is reached or the pool is exhausted. If it cannot be reached, the corpus freeze is REFUSED. SET_P is NEVER filtered toward hard negatives: that would inflate G5 denominator and deflate G6 by construction.
rules.whyNoEnrichmentHere: G5 is class-conditional on the gold hard_negative flag, but the hard-negative SHARE is itself a property of the sample. Enriching it would make G3 precision and G6 needs-review - both estimated on the same SET_P - measurements of an enriched population that production will never see.

rules.question: duplicate and near-duplicate exclusion
rules.rule: EXACT duplicates are removed by documentSha256, as production does. NEAR-duplicates are detected within one organisation only: shingle the redacted extracted main_text into overlapping token 5-grams after whitespace and case normalisation, and compute Jaccard similarity between every pair of that organisation pages. A pair at or above NEAR_DUPLICATE_JACCARD_THRESHOLD = 0.90 contributes AT MOST ONE item - the earlier by the deterministic rank of the sample being drawn.
rules.whyWithinOrganisationOnly: Two different organisations publishing similar pages is a real property of the population and must survive into the sample. Two near-identical pages of ONE organisation are one piece of evidence counted twice.
rules.thresholdClassification: MECHANICAL SAFETY BOUND, NOT A CALIBRATED VALUE. No measurement in this repository calibrates a near-duplicate threshold. It is recorded as uncalibrated and listed in openUnknowns.

rules.question: multilingual-page treatment
rules.rule: declared_lang is recorded per item as the DOCUMENT own declaration and never as a country, market or learner-language signal. Language is a REPORTING stratum, never a gate. A stratum below MIN_SUBGROUP_SIZE_FOR_GATING = 20 is reported with its raw counts and explicitly marked NOT_GATED. A page with no declared language is recorded as UNDECLARED and is NEVER imputed from the organisation country, the URL or the text.
rules.multilingualPagesAreOneItem: A page that declares one language but contains several is ONE item under its declared language. It is never split into per-language items, because the classifier answers per page and a split item would have no model output of its own.
rules.countryIsReportingOnly: The organisation ECHE country code is recorded per item as a REPORTED stratum for generalisation analysis only. It is never a sampling constraint, a gate, a weight or an inference input.

rules.question: acquisition stop, minimum and maximum rules
rules.rule: An organisation is ACQUISITION_SUCCESSFUL iff, after policy-authorised discovery and after SD7 deduplication, it yields at least MIN_PAGES_PER_ORGANISATION = 4 distinct pages with extractable text. Acquisition per organisation is bounded by the already frozen Phase 2B-1e orchestrator budgets and acquires at most MAX_PAGES_ACQUIRED_PER_ORGANISATION = 35 ordinary pages. Acquisition STOPS when 110 ACQUISITION_SUCCESSFUL organisations exist, or when the reserve list is exhausted - in which case the freeze is REFUSED.
rules.maxPagesIsNotANewBudget: MAX_PAGES_ACQUIRED_PER_ORGANISATION reuses the already-frozen Phase 2B-1e ordinary-page budget rather than inventing a second one. Acquisition remains subject to every landed orchestrator bound, robots policy and host gate without exception; this methodology grants no new network authority.
rules.minPagesClassification: MECHANICAL SAFETY BOUND. 4 is the SET_R per-organisation cap: an organisation that cannot fill its enriched allowance contributes an unusable fraction of a cluster.
rules.noAdaptiveStopping: Acquisition never stops early because results look adequate, and never continues because they do not. The stop condition is a count of successful organisations and nothing else. No gold label and no model output exists at acquisition time.

rules.question: semantic-class representation
rules.rule: Every gated semantic sub-class must hold at least MIN_GOLD_ITEMS_PER_GATED_CLASS = 2 gold items in the split. A class below that is REPORTED with its raw counts and explicitly marked NOT_GATED; it is NEVER folded silently into the aggregate and NEVER dropped from the report.
rules.classRepresentationIsNotEngineered: Class representation is MEASURED on the drawn sample and reported. It is not achieved by selecting items on their gold class, which would be gold-aware sampling.

rules.question: representative versus enriched strata
rules.rule: SET_P is the REPRESENTATIVE stratum: prevalence-faithful, class-unfiltered, and the only sample on which a prevalence-dependent quantity may be estimated. SET_R is the ENRICHED stratum: rank-selected on a frozen candidate-independent score, and never read as a population estimate. Every reported metric carries the NAME of the sample it was estimated on, in its own label.
rules.universityWideVersusUnitPages: SET_P is NOT balanced between university-wide and unit-level pages: balancing it would destroy the prevalence G3 and G6 depend on. SET_R records the distinction as a REPORTED stratum so that a recall failure concentrated on one page type is visible, and it is never used to reweight a gate.

rules.question: weighting for prevalence-sensitive metrics
rules.rule: NO WEIGHTING IS USED ANYWHERE. Every weight in Methodology V2 is exactly 1.
rules.whyNoneIsNeeded: The two-sample design removes the need for weighting: every prevalence-dependent metric (G3, G5, G6) lives entirely on the prevalence-faithful SET_P, and every class-conditional metric (G2, G4) lives on SET_R where prevalence is irrelevant by construction. There is no quantity left that a weight would correct.
rules.ifWeightingWereEverAdopted: The stated precision alternative - stratifying SET_P by the frozen signal score and oversampling the high-score stratum - would require pre-registered weights with KNOWN inclusion probabilities fixed before any draw, and the exact binomial bound would no longer apply to the resulting weighted ratio estimator. It is NOT adopted, and adopting it later would be a new methodology generation, not an amendment.

sectionE_samplingContract.everyRefusalIsARefusalNeverASilentDowngr: Every shortfall rule in this section ends in a REFUSED freeze rather than a smaller corpus, a relaxed cap or a rebalanced stratum. A methodology that silently shrinks to fit what was acquired is the defect this revision exists to remove.

twoPurposesKeptApart.A_productionLikePerformance: estimated on SET_P only, which is prevalence-faithful and unfiltered
twoPurposesKeptApart.B_enoughRarePositivesAndHardNegatives: secured by SET_R, which is enriched and is never read as a population estimate

metricClassification.class: prevalence-independent in intent; the union is used because structured-output validity is a property of the response format. Any prevalence sensitivity it turns out to have is REPORTED as a split between the two samples rather than assumed away.
class-conditional on GOLD = UNIT_PAGE, therefore prevalence-independent; positive enrichment is legitimate and efficient
PREVALENCE-DEPENDENT (conditional on the MODEL predicting UNIT_PAGE). Estimating it on SET_R would inflate it by construction.

class-conditional on the gold hard_negative flag, but the hard-negative SHARE is itself a property of the sample, so it is estimated on the prevalence-faithful sample to keep the denominator meaningful
PREVALENCE-DEPENDENT. An enriched needs-review rate is not a population rate.

sectionF_prevalenceAndEnrichment.noSilentReinterpretation: No enriched precision and no enriched NEEDS_REVIEW prevalence is ever reported as a population quantity. A metric estimated on SET_R carries its sample name in its own reported label.

sectionG_devConfirmInformationBoundary.principle: DEV_CONFIRM must not become DEV_TRAIN through repeated inspection.
sectionG_devConfirmInformationBoundary.ownerInstruction: owner instruction section 7: DEV_CONFIRM INFORMATION BOUNDARY
sectionG_devConfirmInformationBoundary.narrowedFromR1: R1 permitted the study-level outcome, the structural-precondition outcomes, the realised denominators and the feasibility re-check results. R2 NARROWS the surface to the owner-enumerated five categories below. Where R1 was wider, R2 is the operative rule.
permittedAfterEachCandidateDEV_CONFIRMEv: the terminal outcome token: ACCEPT / REJECT / INADMISSIBLE
the attempt consumption state: CONSUMED / NOT_CONSUMED
forbiddenByExtension: any listing, count or property that identifies WHICH items failed
per-organisation breakdowns, which at a per-organisation cap of 4 to 8 would come close to naming items
per-language, per-class or per-stratum failure breakdowns at any granularity that isolates items
any diff between two candidates per-item results
sectionG_devConfirmInformationBoundary.forbiddenByExtensionRationale: The owner forbidden list names the seven direct disclosures. The extensions above are the same prohibition applied to indirect routes to the same information: a per-organisation breakdown at a cap of 8 pages is an item listing in aggregate clothing.
sectionG_devConfirmInformationBoundary.richerFeedbackJustification: NOT proposed. Richer feedback is what turns a confirmation split into a training split, and with a three-candidate budget the multiplicity argument only holds if each candidate is designed without knowledge of which confirmation items the previous one failed. Any exception would have to explain how candidate 3 is still independent evidence, and R2 has no such explanation to offer.
sectionG_devConfirmInformationBoundary.burnRule: any inspection of a DEV_CONFIRM item by a prompt author permanently moves that item to DEV_TRAIN and it must be replaced from reserve before the next scoring; the replacement is drawn by the same frozen deterministic rank

budget.methodologyGenerationClosedMeans: A new prompt may continue only under a NEW methodology generation with a NEW DEV_CONFIRM set drawn from organisations never previously used, and a NEW FINAL_HOLDOUT. No fourth candidate is evaluated against this generation DEV_CONFIRM under any circumstance.
budget.inadmissibleDoesNotConsumeASlot: WITHDRAWN AS A GENERAL STATEMENT IN R3. It is true ONLY of a PRE_SEMANTIC_INADMISSIBLE attempt - one that became inadmissible while SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED was still FALSE. Such an attempt measured nothing about the candidate and the byte-identical frozen candidate may be retried once the structural or preflight defect is repaired. A POST_SEMANTIC_INADMISSIBLE attempt DOES consume a slot and may never be re-run against this generation. See sectionO_attemptConsumption.
budget.inadmissibleIsNotAnEscapeHatch: A study may never be declared INADMISSIBLE because its results were unwelcome. Admissibility is decided by the structural preconditions S1-S7 against durable evidence, never by an author preference. R3 also removes the incentive: a POST_SEMANTIC_INADMISSIBLE attempt costs a slot exactly as an ACCEPT or a REJECT does, so there is nothing to gain by seeking one.
budget.correctionOfTheR2Wording: R2 justified the refund by saying INADMISSIBLE 'is determined by the structural preconditions S1-S7 alone, all of which are properties of the harness and the corpus rather than of the candidate answers'. The final clause is FALSE - S3 realised feasibility can depend on candidate-produced denominators, and S1 and S4 are only knowable after execution - and it is corrected in sectionA_terminology and sectionO_attemptConsumption.

theTwoProceduralTokens.whyBothAreNeeded: The terminal token alone is not enough to operate D5 budget under R3, because an INADMISSIBLE attempt may be either consumed or not. The consumption token answers exactly that and nothing else.

theR2AdditionWasApproved.whatR2Proposed: the terminal study outcome token: ACCEPT, REJECT or INADMISSIBLE
theR2AdditionWasApproved.r2Status: surfaced as a decision point rather than folded into the permitted list
theR2AdditionWasApproved.ownerDecision: APPROVED in the R3 instruction section 1
theR2AdditionWasApproved.consequence: It is now part of the permitted surface, together with the CONSUMED / NOT_CONSUMED token R3 adds alongside it. There is no longer any proposed addition awaiting owner confirmation, so the list is empty.

methodologyV2FinalHoldout.statusToday: FINAL_HOLDOUT does not exist. It is not acquired, not labelled, not hashed and not enumerated. This document opens nothing and creates nothing.
requirements: must be NEWLY ACQUIRED - no historical file is eligible
dual-reviewed under the section-I contract before use
inaccessible to prompt development: no item, document, label, per-item result or pre-freeze aggregate
cryptographically sealed - a corpus content hash and a split-scoped manifest committed BEFORE any candidate capable of reaching it exists
ONE-SHOT for exactly one selected candidate configuration
accessed only after that candidate has PASSED DEV_CONFIRM and is frozen, and after a separate explicit owner HOLDOUT authorisation naming that exact candidate
RETIRED after either PASS or FAIL

oneShotSemantics.retiredOnEitherOutcome: The HOLDOUT is retired once a semantic attempt has been made against it, at terminal closure, whether the outcome is ACCEPT, REJECT or INADMISSIBLE. A PASS retires it because it has been used; a FAIL retires it because everything learned from a failure is exactly what would contaminate a second attempt; a POST-SEMANTIC INADMISSIBLE retires it because the items were exposed to the candidate regardless of whether a conclusion emerged.
onFailure: no threshold may be changed and re-run against it
no prompt may be changed and re-run against it
no rerun after a provider or runtime terminal failure
any future candidate requires a NEW methodology generation and a fresh, previously unseen FINAL_HOLDOUT
oneShotSemantics.familyOfOneNeedsNoMultiplicityCorrection: The original proposal HOLDOUT multiplicity budget of 3 is REPLACED by strict one-shot, so its Bonferroni argument is moot.
oneShotSemantics.retirementIsKeyedOnSEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STAR: Consumption and retirement are decided by the section-O boundary, not by the terminal outcome. A purely PRE-SEMANTIC inadmissible attempt does NOT retire the HOLDOUT and the byte-identical selected candidate may retry after the defect is repaired.

whatIsReturnedOnFailure.surface: the terminal outcome token, the attempt consumption state, and the same pre-authorised aggregate surface as a failed DEV_CONFIRM (section G). No item-level information of any kind.
whatIsReturnedOnFailure.aPostSemanticInadmissibleIsNotASemanticF: It means NO VALID HOLDOUT CONCLUSION and THE HOLDOUT IS RETIRED. It is neither a pass nor a refutation, and no downstream decision may treat the candidate as having survived a HOLDOUT test.

methodologyV2FinalHoldout.sealedFileDiscipline: DEV_CONFIRM and FINAL_HOLDOUT labels MUST live in split-scoped files. The historical mixed 72-record and 160-record files are exactly why the boundary event in section B could happen at all: a development aggregate could not be computed without opening bytes that also contained holdout rows.

whichSplitsRequireDualReview.DEV_TRAIN: NO. Its labels are working material for diagnosis and certify nothing.

workflow.step1_reviewerA: Reviewer A labels independently from the frozen rubric and the frozen document. A sees no model output, no metric, no threshold and no gate outcome.
workflow.step2_reviewerB: Reviewer B labels independently and BLIND TO A: the tooling presents the item in the same frozen form and records B label without ever displaying A label. B likewise sees no model output, no metric, no threshold and no gate outcome.
workflow.step3_agreementRecorded: A per-item agree/disagree record, plus percent agreement and Cohen kappa over the dual-reviewed set, committed with the corpus and RECOMPUTED in CI so a later edit cannot silently change them.
workflow.step4_adjudication: ONLY disagreements reach adjudication. The adjudicator sees the frozen document, the rubric and the two ANONYMISED candidate labels - and no model output, no metric, no gate outcome and no threshold effect.
workflow.step5_provenance: Final gold provenance binds BOTH source labels and, where adjudication occurred, the adjudication record: the two anonymised labels, the adjudicated verdict and the adjudicator actor_key. A gold label whose provenance does not name both source labels is not conformant.

whoMayAdjudicate.specification: ADJUDICATION MAY BE PERFORMED BY EITHER THE OWNER OR AN INDEPENDENT THIRD HUMAN REVIEWER. Owner adjudication is NOT required. The choice is made per corpus, recorded in the corpus manifest before labelling begins, and may not change after labels are collected.
constraintsOnAnyAdjudicator: must be HUMAN - no model output may define, confirm or adjudicate gold
must NOT have been reviewer A or reviewer B for that item
must see only the frozen document, the rubric and the two anonymised labels
must see no model output, no metric, no gate outcome and no threshold effect
is recorded per item as an OPAQUE actor_key matching ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{2,63}$ - never a name, a mailbox or a handle
whoMayAdjudicate.actorKeyConventionSource: the same opaque-slug convention migration 0007 uses for root-promotion audit fields: it names WHICH TRUSTED PATH acted, never who.
whoMayAdjudicate.whyTheOwnerIsNotForcedIntoTheLoop: The design deliberately minimises owner work: full review of the small high-stakes class, sampling for the large low-stakes class, and adjudication only where two humans disagreed - roughly 36 items across the whole Option B corpus at 90% agreement. Requiring the owner personally would make the corpus hostage to one person availability without improving the label, since the adjudicator sees exactly the same blinded material either way.

scope.fullDualReview: ALL gold UNIT_PAGE items in the two gated splits - the rare, high-stakes, gate-carrying class
scope.sampledDualReview: a random 15% sample of gold negatives, drawn by the frozen salted rank sha256("DUAL_REVIEW_V2_R2:" + goldId) ascending
scope.purposeOfTheNegativeSample: to MEASURE label error rate and inter-rater agreement, which have never been measured anywhere in this repository - there is no second annotator, no percent agreement and no kappa in the history, and the only blinded review that exists covered exactly one item

whatNeedsNoHuman: every deterministic or provenance-derived field: goldId, documentSha256, split assignment, language stratum, discovery method, track membership, sparse and truncated flags
whatRequiresHumanConfirmation: unit_type on every gold UNIT_PAGE item
sectionI_goldAndReviewContract.whyFrozenProvenanceCannotAnswerThese: The deterministic signal layer cannot separate a UNIT from a DEGREE PROGRAMME - that separation is the entire reason the semantic classifier exists (ADR 0007). No deterministic rule can supply the label the classifier is graded against.
sectionI_goldAndReviewContract.secondReviewerMustBeHuman: No model output may define or confirm gold. If no second human is available, the corpus records UNMEASURED_LABEL_ERROR as a stated limitation - never a fabricated agreement statistic. A corpus carrying UNMEASURED_LABEL_ERROR is NOT conformant for a gated split.
sectionI_goldAndReviewContract.noFabrication: an item whose correct label cannot be determined from its own captured evidence is labelled NEEDS_REVIEW or excluded with its reason recorded; it is never guessed
sectionI_goldAndReviewContract.historicalLabelsAreNotUpgraded: The 49 historical DEVELOPMENT labels stay as they are, in DEV_TRAIN_DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY. Re-reviewing them would spend the scarce human budget on a split that certifies nothing.

splits.name: DEV_TRAIN
splits.promptAuthorsMayInspect: everything - items, documents, gold labels, rationales, full model outputs, per-item results
splits.purpose: candidate design and diagnosis; unlimited iteration

splits.name: DEV_CONFIRM
splits.promptAuthorsMayInspect: NOTHING beyond the section-G feedback surface

splits.name: FINAL_HOLDOUT
splits.purpose: the single confirmatory test before Phase 2E eligibility

sectionJ_splits.disjointness: STRICTLY ORGANISATION-DISJOINT. No organisation may appear in more than one split. This is a deliberate reversal of PHASE_2B_2D_GOLD_CORPUS_PROTOCOL.md section 17 ("every organisation contributes to both sides").
sectionJ_splits.disjointnessIsStructural: SD2 assigns each organisation exactly one split by its selection index, so an organisation cannot appear twice by construction. Overlap is not merely forbidden - there is no procedure that could produce it. S5 re-checks it at scoring time anyway.

historicalDevelopmentSet.rationale: its labels are already burned by five successive iterations of inspection, which is exactly what a training split is for; discarding it would waste real adjudicated evidence, and promoting it would launder adaptive reuse into a decision

sectionJ_splits.historicalEvidenceImmutable: F5, F6 and F9 evidence remains immutable and is reinterpreted nowhere in this document. The canonical F9 result DEV_NOT_READY_FOR_HOLDOUT stands.

sectionK_feasibilityPrecondition.rule: A study freeze is INVALID unless, for EVERY gate, all of the following hold at the PLANNED denominator - and the same check is repeated at the REALISED denominator after scoring, where a failure makes that metric INADMISSIBLE rather than a pass or a fail.

conditions.name: FEASIBLE
conditions.rule: certificationBoundary(rule).feasible === true - some attainable observation certifies the gate

conditions.name: NON-DEGENERATE
conditions.rule: criticalCount is strictly inside the denominator, so the gate tolerates at least one error. A gate whose critical count equals its denominator is a zero-tolerance gate wearing a percentage label, which is defect d2 of the original diagnosis. G1 is the ONE declared exception, because it is frozen as a zero-tolerance gate honestly and explicitly.

conditions.name: CLUSTER-ESTIMABLE
conditions.rule: the gate own denominator draws on at least MIN_ORGANISATIONS_PER_GATE = 10 organisations, so an intraclass correlation can be estimated at all

conditions.name: CLASS MINIMUM
conditions.rule: any gated sub-class has at least 2 gold items; a class with fewer is REPORTED and explicitly NOT GATED

conditions.name: NON-VACUOUS
conditions.rule: a gate whose denominator is 0 is INADMISSIBLE for that metric, never a pass - a change from the frozen metrics.ts behaviour, where a vacuous gate returns pass: true

sectionK_feasibilityPrecondition.minOrganisationsClassification: MECHANICAL SAFETY BOUND, NOT A CALIBRATED VALUE. It is deliberately NOT the original proposal 30: that 30 existed because a percentile cluster bootstrap is unreliable below it, and the bootstrap is demoted to reporting.
sectionK_feasibilityPrecondition.certifyMeansTheApprovedD2Method: K1 and K2 are evaluated under the APPROVED D2 method of section C.

everyCurrentlyFrozenGateFailsThisCheckAt.classification: METHODOLOGICAL CONTEXT. These are properties of thresholds and denominators, computed without reference to any candidate result.

theSixth.note: G6 is the ONE frozen gate that passes K1 at the historical denominator. It fails no feasibility test; it was simply absent from the original proposal table.

sectionL_replicationAndStability.addresses: owner instruction section 2: FULL N = 5 REPLICATION IS RETIRED

fullNFiveReplication.ownerInstruction: Do NOT carry the old N=5 full-study replication into Methodology V2.
fullNFiveReplication.notRetiredByInertia: The frozen N = 5 was, on the record, a judgement anchored on an owner default for a TWO-ARM DIAGNOSTIC study and transferred unexamined to a ONE-ARM ACCEPTANCE study.

theDecisiveArithmetic.atAFixedInferenceBudget: with budget B = n * R, the variance becomes (R * betweenItemVariance + withinItemVariance) / B, which is STRICTLY INCREASING in R
theDecisiveArithmetic.consequence: Spending a fixed inference budget on more ITEMS always beats spending it on more REPLICATES, for the quality question. This holds for every positive value of both variance components, so it needs no measurement of either.

theTwoQuantitiesSeparated.datasetUncertainty: how far the estimate could be from the truth because THESE organisations and pages were sampled rather than others. Governed by the denominator and by clustering. Replication does not reduce it at all.
theTwoQuantitiesSeparated.modelStochasticity: how far a single run could be from the candidate own expected behaviour because the provider is not deterministic. Governed by the number of inferences per item.
theTwoQuantitiesSeparated.theGatesMeasureTheFirst: the six semantic gates answer the dataset question; the stability subset answers the second, and they are never mixed

mainPass.appliesTo: the FULL frozen split - every item of SET_P union SET_R
mainPass.noGateReadsAStabilityReplicate: The three stability calls never enter a gate numerator or denominator. A gate is computed once, on the main pass. Averaging a gate across replicates, or taking its best or worst replicate, is forbidden.

stabilitySubset.replicatesTotalIncludesTheMainPass: R = 3 TOTAL means the main pass plus 2 additional passes over the subset. The extra inference cost per gated split is therefore 80 calls, not 120.
stabilitySubset.neverChosenOnModelErrors: The subset is a deterministic function of the committed corpus and gold labels alone. No model output, no error list, no failing item and no candidate result participates in its selection, and none exists when it is computed.
stabilitySubset.itemsNeverSurfacedToPromptAuthors: The subset item identities are never shown to a prompt author; only the aggregate statistics ST1-ST3 cross the seal (section G).

selectionAlgorithm.step1_frame: the frozen evaluation set of the split: SET_P union SET_R, deduplicated by goldId
selectionAlgorithm.step2_strata: Partition the frame by GOLD class into exactly three strata, in this frozen processing order: (1) GOLD_UNIT_PAGE - gold verdict UNIT_PAGE; (2) GOLD_HARD_NEGATIVE - gold verdict not UNIT_PAGE and the gold hard_negative flag set; (3) GOLD_OTHER - every remaining item, which is the non-hard negatives together with gold NEEDS_REVIEW.
selectionAlgorithm.step4_withinStratumRank: Rank the stratum members by sha256("STABILITY_V2_R2:" + goldId) ascending, lower-case hex, lexicographic.
selectionAlgorithm.step5_walk: Process the three strata in the frozen order above. Within a stratum, walk the rank from position 0 and select an item unless its organisation already holds STABILITY_MAX_ITEMS_PER_ORGANISATION = 2 items across the WHOLE subset selected so far; skipped items are passed over, never reordered. Stop that stratum at its quota.
selectionAlgorithm.step6_shortfall: If any stratum cannot reach its quota under the organisation cap, the STUDY FREEZE IS REFUSED. Quotas are never rebalanced between strata, the cap is never relaxed, and a subset smaller than 40 is never accepted.
selectionAlgorithm.whyNoSeed: The rank is a content hash over the committed goldId, so the permutation is fixed by the corpus itself. There is no pseudo-random stream, therefore no seed to freeze. This is recorded explicitly because the owner instruction requires the exact seed IF sampling is seeded - it is not.

stabilitySubset.organisationStratificationConsequence: A cap of 2 over a 40-item subset guarantees at least 20 distinct organisations, which is twice MIN_ORGANISATIONS_PER_GATE. Run-to-run agreement is therefore measured across organisations, not inside two or three of them.
stabilitySubset.quotaFeasibilityUnderOptionB: Per gated split Option B guarantees at least 100 gold UNIT_PAGE items and at least 155 gold hard negatives, against quotas of 16 and 16; GOLD_OTHER draws on the remainder of a 360-item SET_P against a quota of 8. All three quotas are comfortably feasible, and the organisation cap of 2 across 45 organisations permits up to 90 selections against a subset of 40.
stabilitySubset.classStratificationRationale: The quotas deliberately over-represent the two classes that carry the highest-stakes gates relative to their population share, because the subset measures DISPERSION, not prevalence. The subset is never used to estimate any population quantity, so its non-representativeness costs nothing and its class coverage buys everything.

metrics.name: perItemAllReplicateAgreementRate
metrics.definition: the number of subset items on which ALL 3 replicates produced the identical page-level verdict, divided by 40

metrics.name: unitTypeAllReplicateAgreementRate
metrics.definition: among subset items on which all 3 replicates answered UNIT_PAGE, the number on which all 3 also produced the identical unit_type, divided by that count
metrics.notGatedBelowTwo: a denominator below 2 is REPORTED and explicitly NOT used by the veto

metrics.name: gatedMetricRange
metrics.definition: for each of the five RATE gates G2-G6, recompute the metric on the 40-item subset alone within each replicate, then report max minus min across the 3 replicates, together with all three per-replicate values
metrics.reportedWith: the three per-replicate values, not only the range
metrics.thisIsADispersionMeasurementNotAGate: A metric recomputed on 16 subset items is not a gate and is never certified. It is a dispersion statistic and is labelled as one.

whatIsNeverDone: no gate is averaged across replicates
no gate takes its best or its worst replicate
the three replicates are never treated as three independent datasets
no stability statistic is folded into a quality metric
no replicate is replaced, retried or discarded
a failed stability replicate never refunds the candidate attempt

instabilityVeto.rule: REJECT the candidate if ST1 < 0.90 OR max over the five rate gates of ST3 range > 0.10
instabilityVeto.canOnlyReject: V_STAB can only REJECT. It can never rescue a candidate whose gate or bound fails, it is never averaged into a quality metric, and passing it certifies nothing.
instabilityVeto.toleranceClassification: OWNER_DESIGN_DECISION and MECHANICAL SAFETY BOUND - NOT CALIBRATED
instabilityVeto.toleranceHonesty: Neither 0.90 nor 0.10 is derived from any measurement in this repository. No measurement here calibrates a dispersion tolerance, and R2 does not invent one and dress it up. R1 declined to freeze a veto at all for exactly this reason and proposed a report-only flag; the owner instruction requires an exact instability veto, so R2 freezes one and declares both constants uncalibrated rather than leaving the requirement unmet or the numbers unlabelled.
instabilityVeto.r1FlagPromoted: R1's INSTABILITY_OBSERVED flag (agreement below 0.90 or a metric range above 0.10) is promoted to this veto at the same two numbers. The numbers did not change; their FORCE did, by owner instruction.
instabilityVeto.instabilityIsAlreadyPenalisedOnceHonestl: An unstable candidate single main-pass run is as likely to be its bad run as its good one, so instability already shows up as a lower expected point estimate. V_STAB is a second, explicit line of defence, not the only one.
instabilityVeto.replicateCountIsExact: R must be exactly 3 on the subset. A replicate that reaches a terminal failure makes the STUDY INADMISSIBLE; V_STAB is never computed from 2 replicates, and a failed replicate is never replaced. Because the main pass necessarily crossed SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED before any stability replicate could run, such a study is POST_SEMANTIC_INADMISSIBLE and CONSUMES the attempt - it is never re-run against the same gated split. See sectionO_attemptConsumption.stabilityExecution.

noCatastrophicReplicateGate.ownerInstruction: Do NOT introduce a 'catastrophic replicate' gate copied from the old N=5 method.
noCatastrophicReplicateGate.notDeferredNotOptional: R1 kept a catastrophic-replicate rule as a candidate for review. R2 REMOVES it outright. It is not defined, not frozen and not available to be switched on.
noCatastrophicReplicateGate.whyItCouldNotWorkHere: Under an R = 1 main pass the rule has NO DENOMINATOR - there are no full-split replicates for it to range over. Applied instead to the 40-item stability subset it would re-create the original defect at small scale: at n = 40 the recall gate critical count equals its denominator, so a catastrophic-replicate test there would be a zero-tolerance test wearing a percentage label.

organisationLevelCatastropheVeto.status: RETAINED - unchanged in substance from R1
organisationLevelCatastropheVeto.ownerInstruction: Retain the organisation-level catastrophe veto from R1 if already precisely defined and substantively justified.
organisationLevelCatastropheVeto.precisionCheck: PRECISELY DEFINED - the rule below has an exact denominator, an exact numerator and an exact threshold
organisationLevelCatastropheVeto.justificationCheck: SUBSTANTIVELY JUSTIFIED - it names a downstream failure mode no frozen metric expresses
organisationLevelCatastropheVeto.rule: the count of ORGANISATIONS that have at least one gold UNIT_PAGE item in the split but from which the candidate recalls no UNIT_PAGE at all must be 0
organisationLevelCatastropheVeto.denominator: organisations in the split holding at least one gold UNIT_PAGE item
organisationLevelCatastropheVeto.rationale: This is the downstream failure the product cannot absorb: an organisation with no recalled unit page is silently dropped from the pipeline and is unrecoverable later. A page-level miss whose sibling page is recalled is recoverable. No frozen metric expresses this, because no frozen metric has an organisation denominator.
organisationLevelCatastropheVeto.classification: STRUCTURAL VETO derived from the downstream failure mode, not from any candidate behaviour
organisationLevelCatastropheVeto.evaluatedOn: the single main pass. R1 original "in at least ceil(R/2) replicates" qualifier is dropped because it presupposed full replication, which is retired.

costComparisonAtCorpusOptionB.ratio: approximately 4.4x fewer provider calls, for MORE item evidence, because the saved budget is what pays for the larger denominator in the first place

sectionM_acceptanceRuleShape.appliesTo: one FROZEN candidate evaluated on one named split

stages.name: structural preconditions
stages.conditions: the seven preconditions S1-S7 of section A
stages.note: INADMISSIBLE is not REJECT: it says the study produced no valid conclusion, so nothing may be concluded about the candidate in either direction. It does NOT follow that nothing was MEASURED. An attempt that crossed SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED before failing has executed the candidate against sealed items, and consumes its attempt accordingly (section O).
stages.someConditionsAreOnlyEvaluablePostSemant: S1 and S4 are POST-SEMANTIC; S3, S5, S6 and S7 are BOTH; only S2 is purely PRE-SEMANTIC.

stages.name: structural vetoes
stages.note: Neither veto is a semantic gate and neither counts toward the six. Both can only reject.

stages.name: the six semantic gates
stages.conditions: G1-G6 under the approved D2 method of section C, each at its own denominator with its own per-gate design effect

stages.name: stability reporting
stages.failureOutcome: none - ST1, ST2 and ST3 are reported here; their VETO force is applied at stage 1 as V_STAB

stages.name: aggregation

invariants.noPooling: results from different splits, different methodology generations or different reliability-semantics versions are never pooled

missingnessSemantics.infrastructureInvalid: a non-terminal provider timeout or transport failure is INFRASTRUCTURE, not a semantic property of the candidate. Its items are excluded from SEMANTIC denominators, reported separately with their exact count, and capped by S4.
missingnessSemantics.changeFromFrozen: the frozen semantics score an infrastructure-caused INVALID item as a strict semantic miss, which makes the gate partly a measurement of the host and the network
missingnessSemantics.assumptionStated: this exclusion is unbiased only if infrastructure failure is independent of item difficulty. That is plausible for a transport timeout but is UNMEASURED, and is recorded as a METHODOLOGICAL ASSUMPTION rather than a fact.
missingnessSemantics.candidateInvalid: a validator rejection surviving the one bounded ADR 0011 repair round is a genuine candidate output failure and fails gate G1
missingnessSemantics.terminalFailure: a replicate reaching a terminal failure makes the STUDY INADMISSIBLE; it is never scored as a partial result. If the terminal failure occurred after SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED, the attempt is CONSUMED (section O).
missingnessSemantics.realisedDenominatorBelowPlan: INADMISSIBLE for that metric - never a pass and never a fail. Where the realised denominator is derived from candidate outputs - G3 unitPagePrecision above all - the failure is POST-SEMANTIC by definition and ALWAYS CONSUMES the attempt; it is explicitly not a harness-only failure.
missingnessSemantics.consumptionIsGovernedBySectionO: Missingness decides admissibility. It does not decide consumption: that is decided by SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED alone.

sectionO_attemptConsumption.title: SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED and attempt consumption
sectionO_attemptConsumption.whyThisSectionExists: R2 asserted that an INADMISSIBLE study "measured nothing about the candidate", and therefore that the same frozen candidate could always be re-run. That is TOO BROAD and is the one defect R3 corrects. An attempt can become INADMISSIBLE AFTER semantic execution has begun - a terminal provider failure part-way through, a stability replicate that dies, or a realised denominator that turns out infeasible only because of what the candidate predicted. Those attempts HAVE measured the candidate, and granting them a free retry would hand a prompt author an unlimited supply of attempts against a sealed split by the simple expedient of a study that fails late.
sectionO_attemptConsumption.theCorrectedClaim: SOME inadmissible attempts measured nothing about the candidate. Others measured it and then failed to produce a reportable conclusion. Only the first kind may be retried.

boundary.type: MONOTONIC - once TRUE it can never return to FALSE
boundary.definedAs: TRUE when a real provider request, a semantic model execution, or an accepted semantic output has occurred for this attempt - whichever is earliest.
boundary.monotonicityIsStructural: The flag is derived from APPEND-ONLY evidence: Postgres rows under a role with no UPDATE or DELETE grant, and write-once fsync-ed artifacts whose writer refuses an overwrite (WriteOnceCollisionError). A value that can only be set by the appearance of a record, over stores that admit no deletion, cannot be unset.

notANewInvention.statement: SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED is the Methodology V2 name for a boundary this repository has already frozen, already named, and already corrected once in the light of a real failure. R3 adopts it rather than inventing a second one.
notANewInvention.existingRule: the F0V predeclared inclusion rule, CLASS C
notANewInvention.existingRuleMeaningVerbatim: Any provider request or semantic execution occurred for the slot.
notANewInvention.existingRuleActionVerbatim: That slot is IRREVOCABLY part of the study, whether it completes successfully or ends in a genuine terminal failure/halt. Never replaced or discarded. This is the predeclared inclusion rule.
existingVocabulary: SEMANTIC_EXECUTION_MARKER_FILE_NAMES - the irreversible semantic-execution marker set
notANewInvention.whyReuseRatherThanRedefine: The owner instruction says to prefer the earliest EXISTING durable event and not to invent a later boundary for convenience. F0V Class C already is that event, it is already irrevocable, and it was predeclared rather than chosen after seeing results. Defining a second boundary would put two incompatible irrevocability rules in one repository.

theArchitectureHasTwoDurableSystems.warning: The production classifier and the study harness keep separate durable records and do not share a store. The boundary is defined over BOTH, and an attempt is STARTED if either system shows it.

systems.preRequestRecord: orgunit_classifier_calls - one row per attempted invocation
systems.writtenRelativeToTheRequest: STRICTLY BEFORE - the row is inserted before the provider is invoked
systems.schemaIntentVerbatim: One attempted semantic-classifier INVOCATION, recorded before the provider answers - configuration only. This row is never authority for anything: it names an ATTEMPT, not a result.
systems.positiveExecutionEvidence: orgunit_page_classifications (an accepted semantic output), or an orgunit_classifier_call_completions row whose terminal state is not a pre-inference refusal
systems.appendOnly: the nwf_classifier role holds no UPDATE or DELETE grant on these tables

systems.system: STUDY HARNESS (write-once fsync-ed JSON artifacts; touches no database at all)
systems.preRequestRecord: child-preflight.json with ok true and providerConstructed false
systems.writtenRelativeToTheRequest: STRICTLY BEFORE - the last durable write before the provider is constructed
systems.positiveExecutionEvidence: any member of SEMANTIC_EXECUTION_MARKER_FILE_NAMES - raw-output-checkpoint.json, provider-outcome.json, validation-result.json, tier1-diagnostics.json, child-result.json, repair-round.json
systems.appendOnly: writeFileOnceDurably refuses an overwrite; an existing path is a collision error, never a rewrite

aCallRowIsNecessaryButNotSUFFICIENT.rule: The existence of a pre-request record - an orgunit_classifier_calls row, or a passing child-preflight - does NOT by itself make SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED true. It records an INTENT to dispatch, not a dispatch.
twoWaysAPreRequestRecordExistsWithZeroSe: a provider PRE-FLIGHT or auth refusal: the runner is never invoked, and the call is completed as an auth failure with no request issued
a bounded repair whose budget decides SKIP: the repair call row records the DECISION, the provider is never invoked, and the completion records the skip
aCallRowIsNecessaryButNotSUFFICIENT.thereforeTheBoundaryRequiresPositiveEvid: SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED is set by POSITIVE evidence of execution, not by the absence of a refusal record. This is the F0V Class C reading, and it is the corrected one.

theMeasuredReasonThisBoundaryIsNotPlaced.whatHappened: An earlier implementation of exactly this boundary treated ANY artifact written past parent child-manifest construction as semantic execution. On 2026-09-16 the first real F0X study invocation exposed it: all ten children refused at their own freeze stage with providerConstructed false, zero provider requests and zero adapter attempts - yet every slot read as SEMANTIC EXECUTION OBSERVED, and the study advanced through all ten candidates.
theMeasuredReasonThisBoundaryIsNotPlaced.whatItCost: ten candidate slots spent for zero semantic evidence
theMeasuredReasonThisBoundaryIsNotPlaced.theCorrection: the sequencing module was rewritten to require a POSITIVE semantic-execution marker, and to classify the undecidable middle as AMBIGUOUS_EVIDENCE that BLOCKS rather than advances
theMeasuredReasonThisBoundaryIsNotPlaced.whyThisGovernsR3: A rule that sets SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED at the pre-request record would reproduce that incident exactly, and would do it while burning the three-attempt DEV_CONFIRM budget and the one-shot FINAL_HOLDOUT. R3 therefore places the boundary where the repository already learned it belongs.

theDurabilityGap.statement: NO durable record anywhere in this architecture is written at the instant the request is issued. Between the last pre-request record and the first post-response marker there is a window spanning the entire network call in which a crash leaves no durable trace of whether a request went out.
theDurabilityGap.existingBehaviour: The harness already refuses to guess inside that window: a child that passed preflight, so the provider factory was reachable, but wrote no semantic-execution marker, is classified AMBIGUOUS_EVIDENCE and BLOCKS. It neither advances the study nor releases the slot.

resolution.rule: SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED is THREE-VALUED at classification time and TWO-VALUED at closure.

states.evidence: positive semantic-execution evidence exists in either durable system (F0V Class C)
positively demonstrated absence: a confirmed pre-inference refusal with the provider never constructed, zero recorded provider requests, and no semantic-execution marker (F0V Class A or Class B)
the durability gap - a request can be neither confirmed nor excluded
states.consumption: BLOCKED - no automatic classification in either direction
states.action: The attempt is HALTED and preserved. It is neither counted against the budget nor released for retry until a separate owner adjudication classifies it. No retry of the candidate against that split may occur while an attempt is AMBIGUOUS.
states.adjudicationDefault: If the evidence cannot settle the question, the adjudication resolves to CONSUMED. The default runs toward spending the attempt, never toward releasing it.

resolution.whyNotJustAutoConsumeOnAmbiguity: Because that is precisely the 2026-09-16 defect: ten slots were consumed for ten refusals that provably issued nothing. Auto-consuming an ambiguous attempt makes every harness crash cost a candidate, which punishes infrastructure faults with methodology budget.
resolution.whyNotJustAutoRefundOnAmbiguity: Because that is the loophole R3 exists to close: a prompt author would obtain unlimited attempts against a sealed split by ensuring the harness dies before it writes a marker.
resolution.whyBlockingIsTheHonestAnswer: Neither automatic answer is defensible, so R3 does not pick one silently. It halts, preserves the evidence, and puts the decision in front of the owner with the default already set against the candidate. Blocking cannot be gamed - it yields no retry - and it cannot silently burn a provable refusal.
resolution.ambiguityIsExpectedToBeRare: It requires a crash inside the request window specifically. It is not a routine state, and a corpus generation that produced many of them would itself be evidence of an unfit execution environment.

theTable.note: an accepted study necessarily executed semantically
a rejected study necessarily executed semantically
nothing about the candidate was measured, so nothing about it was learned
the candidate WAS measured; the study merely failed to yield a reportable conclusion

theAmbiguousCase.consumption: BLOCKED pending owner adjudication; default on adjudication is CONSUMED
theAmbiguousCase.note: A crash inside the durability gap leaves a request neither confirmed nor excluded. The attempt is halted and preserved; it is neither counted nor released, and the candidate may not retry against that split while it stands. See boundary.resolution.

attemptOutcomeAndConsumption.theOnlyNotConsumedCell: Exactly one of the four rows is NOT_CONSUMED: INADMISSIBLE with SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED false. Every other terminal state consumes the attempt.
attemptOutcomeAndConsumption.consumptionIsAFunctionOfTheBoundaryNotOf: Consumption is decided by SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED alone. The terminal outcome does not decide it; ACCEPT and REJECT merely imply the boundary was crossed.

preSemanticInadmissible.condition: the attempt becomes INADMISSIBLE while SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED is FALSE
rules: the candidate slot is NOT consumed
the SAME EXACT frozen candidate may be retried after the structural or preflight defect is repaired
the candidate bytes and configuration must remain IDENTICAL - a changed candidate is a NEW candidate and consumes a new slot
it does not increment the three-candidate budget
preSemanticInadmissible.candidateIdentityIsEnforcedByHash: Retry is permitted only for a candidate whose prompt version, output schema version and request-configuration hash are byte-identical to the attempt that was refused (structural precondition S6). A retry that changes any of them is not a retry.
examples: wrong split hash caught at preflight
host or runtime readiness refusal before provider construction
an impossible PLANNED denominator discovered before execution
wrong reliability-semantics version caught before dispatch
preSemanticInadmissible.whatMustBeRepairedFirst: the structural or preflight defect itself. A retry that does not repair the defect will simply refuse again, and repeated identical refusals are recorded rather than hidden.
preSemanticInadmissible.noUnboundedRetry: Pre-semantic retries are not free of scrutiny merely because they are free of budget: every refusal is a durable record, and a pattern of refusals is visible to the owner. What they cannot do is leak information about the sealed split, because no item was ever evaluated.

postSemanticInadmissible.condition: SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED is TRUE and the attempt later becomes INADMISSIBLE
rules: it counts toward the maximum of three
that exact candidate may NOT be re-run against this DEV_CONFIRM generation
no replacement attempt for the same slot
no partial score is promoted to ACCEPT or REJECT
postSemanticInadmissible.appliesEvenWithNoReportableMetrics: This holds even if no semantic metric is ultimately reportable. The attempt is consumed because the candidate was EXECUTED against sealed items, not because a number came out.
examples: terminal provider or runtime failure after some semantic evaluations
realised-denominator infeasibility discovered after candidate outputs exist
a G3 precision denominator too small, where the denominator itself depends on candidate predictions
postSemanticInadmissible.noPartialPromotion: A partially-executed study is never scored as if it were complete, and its partial numbers are never promoted to a terminal ACCEPT or REJECT. Structural precondition S1 forbids extrapolation from an observed prefix, and that prohibition is unchanged by R3.
postSemanticInadmissible.whyTheAttemptIsSpentEvenThoughNothingWas: The budget of three exists to bound how many times a sealed split is exposed to a candidate, not to bound how many conclusions are drawn from it. Exposure is what contaminates. A study that executed against 400 sealed items and then crashed has exposed them exactly as much as one that finished.

candidateDeterminedDenominators.rule: A realised-denominator failure discovered FROM CANDIDATE OUTPUTS is POST-SEMANTIC BY DEFINITION, and therefore ALWAYS consumes the attempt.
candidateDeterminedDenominators.neverClassifiedAsHarnessOnly: This is explicitly NOT a harness-only failure. The denominator did not fail because the corpus was wrong or the host was broken; it failed because of what the candidate predicted. Classifying it as infrastructure would be the single most exploitable loophole in the methodology.

theWorkedCase.whyItIsTheExposedOne: G3 is the one gate whose denominator is candidate-determined: it counts the items the candidate ANSWERED UNIT_PAGE. A candidate that answers UNIT_PAGE very rarely shrinks its own G3 denominator.
theWorkedCase.condition: the candidate predicts too few UNIT_PAGE items for the realised G3 denominator to satisfy the section-K feasibility precondition
theWorkedCase.theIncentiveThisCloses: Without this rule a candidate could avoid ever being judged on precision by predicting UNIT_PAGE almost never: the gate would go inadmissible, the attempt would be refunded, and the author could iterate indefinitely against a sealed split. R3 makes that strategy cost a slot every time, which is exactly what it should cost.

candidateDeterminedDenominators.theSameLogicAppliesToAnyFutureCandidateD: G3 is the only such gate today. Any future metric whose denominator depends on candidate output inherits this rule automatically, because the rule is stated over the PROPERTY (candidate-determined) rather than over the gate id.

stabilityExecution.rule: The same spent boundary governs the stability execution. If the main pass has already started semantic execution, the attempt is already CONSUMED, and a stability replicate that later terminates cannot un-consume it.
onAStabilityReplicateTerminalFailure: do NOT re-run that candidate against the same gated split
do NOT replace the failed stability replicate
stabilityExecution.consumption: CONSUMED - the main pass had necessarily already crossed the boundary
stabilityExecution.doesNotResurrectNFiveReplacementLogic: This is NOT the retired N = 5 replacement logic returning. R2 already forbade replacing a replicate; R3 adds only that the failure consumes the attempt rather than refunding it. Nothing here permits a replacement, a retry or a substitution of any replicate.
stabilityExecution.orderingNote: Because the stability subset is drawn from the split the main pass already evaluated, a stability replicate can only run AFTER the main pass has begun. There is therefore no reachable state in which a stability failure is PRE-semantic.

ambiguousAttempts.rule: An attempt whose SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED cannot be resolved from durable evidence is BLOCKED: it is neither counted against the three-attempt budget nor released for retry, and the candidate may not run again against that split until an owner adjudication classifies it.
ambiguousAttempts.whyItCannotBeGamed: Blocking yields no retry, so inducing ambiguity buys a prompt author nothing. It only stops the methodology until a human looks - which is the correct response to evidence that cannot answer the question.

theCounter.name: consumedAttemptCount
theCounter.incrementedBy: exactly 1, at terminal closure of an attempt whose SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED is TRUE
theCounter.notIncrementedByABlockedAmbiguousAttempt: A BLOCKED attempt increments nothing until it is adjudicated. On adjudication it increments by 1 if classified CONSUMED, which is the default.

devConfirmBudget.methodologyGenerationClosedMeans: A new prompt may continue only under a NEW methodology generation with a NEW DEV_CONFIRM set drawn from organisations never previously used, and a NEW FINAL_HOLDOUT. No fourth CONSUMED attempt is evaluated against this generation DEV_CONFIRM under any circumstance.
devConfirmBudget.distinctCandidatesVersusAttempts: Three CONSUMED attempts is the bound, and in the normal case that is three distinct candidates. A candidate that was refused pre-semantically and then retried unchanged has made two attempts and consumed at most one; a candidate whose bytes changed is a different candidate.
devConfirmBudget.inadmissibleIsNotAnEscapeHatch: A study may never be declared INADMISSIBLE because its results were unwelcome. Admissibility is decided by the structural preconditions S1-S7 against durable evidence, never by an author preference, and a POST_SEMANTIC_INADMISSIBLE attempt costs a slot exactly as an ACCEPT or a REJECT does - so there is nothing to gain by seeking one.
devConfirmBudget.thisReplacesTheR2Claim: R2 said an INADMISSIBLE study "measured nothing about the candidate, so the same frozen candidate is re-run after the execution environment is repaired". That is true ONLY for PRE_SEMANTIC_INADMISSIBLE and is withdrawn as a general statement.

beforeTheBoundary.condition: a purely structural or preflight INADMISSIBLE while SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED is FALSE
beforeTheBoundary.rule: A pre-semantic INADMISSIBLE attempt does NOT consume the FINAL_HOLDOUT. The SAME EXACT selected frozen candidate may retry, and only after the pre-semantic defect is repaired.
beforeTheBoundary.noOtherCandidateMayTakeItsPlace: The retry right belongs to the one selected, frozen candidate that earned HOLDOUT access. A different candidate would need to pass DEV_CONFIRM and be selected and authorised in its own right.
beforeTheBoundary.stillRequiresTheOwnerAuthorisationToRema: A pre-semantic refusal may nonetheless have spent the per-run execution authorisation (F0V Class B). The retry then needs a fresh owner authorisation even though the HOLDOUT itself is untouched.

atTheBoundary.rule: Once SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED becomes TRUE for FINAL_HOLDOUT, the FINAL_HOLDOUT is CONSUMED and is RETIRED irreversibly at terminal closure - whether the terminal outcome is ACCEPT, REJECT or INADMISSIBLE.

thereforeForbidden: no second semantic attempt on the same FINAL_HOLDOUT
no rerun after a provider or runtime terminal failure
no new execution of the same candidate against those HOLDOUT items

aPostSemanticInadmissibleHoldoutMeans.thisIsNotAFailedCandidate: A post-semantic INADMISSIBLE FINAL_HOLDOUT is NOT a semantic failure of the candidate and must never be recorded, reported or reasoned about as one. It is the loss of the instrument, not a verdict on the thing being measured. The candidate is neither certified nor refuted.
aPostSemanticInadmissibleHoldoutMeans.andItIsNotAPassEither: Equally it is not a pass. Nothing may be concluded in either direction, and no downstream decision may treat the candidate as having survived a HOLDOUT test.

anyFutureCertificationAttemptRequires: a new methodology generation where required
finalHoldoutRetirement.theHarshnessIsThePoint: Retiring a HOLDOUT on a crash is expensive and is meant to be. A one-shot instrument that can be re-run whenever the first run is inconvenient is not one-shot, and the failure mode it guards against - trying again until the answer is acceptable - does not care whether the first attempt ended in a verdict or in a stack trace.

addedToThePermittedSurfaceInR3: the terminal outcome token: ACCEPT / REJECT / INADMISSIBLE
the attempt consumption state: CONSUMED / NOT_CONSUMED
disclosureSurface.consumptionTokenIsBudgetStateOnly: CONSUMED / NOT_CONSUMED is procedural budget state. It says whether a slot was spent. It says nothing about which items, which organisations, which gates or which outputs were involved.

coarseStructuralReason.surfacedToPromptDevelopment: ONLY IF it cannot reveal sealed item information
coarseStructuralReason.rule: A coarse structural reason MAY be retained internally for audit, but MUST NOT be surfaced to prompt development if it would reveal sealed item information. Where there is doubt about whether a reason leaks, it is withheld.
coarseStructuralReason.workedExample: A realised G3 denominator shortfall is a coarse structural reason, but disclosing it tells a prompt author that the candidate predicted UNIT_PAGE too rarely on THESE sealed items - which is a per-item aggregate about the split. It is therefore withheld from prompt development and retained internally.

disclosureSurface.whyTheConsumptionTokenLeaksNothing: CONSUMED / NOT_CONSUMED is a function of SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED alone, which is a fact about whether a request was issued - not about what any item contained or how the candidate answered. Two studies with identical consumption state may differ arbitrarily in every semantic respect.

structuralPreconditionsAreNotAllPreSeman.theR2WordingThatWasTooStrong: R2 said INADMISSIBLE "is determined by the structural preconditions S1-S7 alone, all of which are properties of the harness and the corpus rather than of the candidate answers". The final clause is FALSE: S3 realised-denominator feasibility can depend on candidate-produced denominators, and S1 completeness and S4 missingness are only knowable once execution has occurred.
theAccurateDistinction: some are PRE-SEMANTIC and can be evaluated before any provider request
some can only be evaluated POST-SEMANTIC, because they range over what execution produced
ADMISSIBILITY IS DISTINCT FROM SEMANTIC QUALITY - an inadmissible study is not a bad candidate
POST-SEMANTIC inadmissibility STILL CONSUMES the attempt
structuralPreconditionsAreNotAllPreSeman.whatChangedIsClassificationOnly: R3 adds an evaluability classification to each of S1-S7 and changes nothing about what any of them requires. The seven-precondition count is unchanged, as the owner instruction requires.

evaluability.name: completeEvidence

evaluability.name: correctReliabilitySemantics
evaluability.why: the declared semantics version is checkable against this build before dispatch

evaluability.name: minimumSampleFeasibility
evaluability.why: PLANNED denominators are checkable pre-semantically at freeze; REALISED denominators are POST-SEMANTIC, and for G3 they depend on candidate predictions

evaluability.name: noForbiddenMissingness
evaluability.why: infrastructure failure counts and terminal failures exist only once execution has been attempted

evaluability.name: correctSplitProvenance
evaluability.why: split membership and organisation-disjointness are checkable at freeze; that EVERY EVALUATED goldId belonged to the declared split is checkable only after evaluation

evaluability.name: candidateFrozenBeforeConfirmation
evaluability.why: the pre-run hash is checkable before dispatch; that it is UNCHANGED AFTER the run is checkable only afterwards

evaluability.name: noExecutionContamination
evaluability.why: the approved auth path and gold-blindness of the inference path are checkable pre-dispatch; tool, MCP, browser and isolation violations are observed during execution

structuralPreconditionsAreNotAllPreSeman.onlyOneIsPurelyPreSemantic: S2 alone is purely pre-semantic. That is precisely why R2 blanket claim was wrong, and why a rule keyed on "which precondition failed" would have been the wrong rule. R3 keys on SEMANTIC_ATTEMPT_STARTED instead, which is a fact about execution rather than about which check noticed the problem.
structuralPreconditionsAreNotAllPreSeman.whyTheBoundaryIsKeyedOnExecutionNotOnPre: A precondition classified BOTH can fail either before or after the boundary. Keying consumption on the precondition id would give the same failure two different costs depending on nothing that matters. Keying it on whether the candidate was executed gives the same failure the same cost every time.
